meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: immediately, as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined
facts.summary: Michigan: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due immediately, as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined.
facts.evidence_quote: (2) An employer shall immediately pay to an employee who has been discharged from employment all wages earned and due, as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined.

facts.value: as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined
facts.summary: Michigan: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined.
facts.evidence_quote: (1) An employer shall pay to an employee voluntarily leaving employment all wages earned and due, as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined.

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Michigan basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $13.73.
facts.evidence_quote: Applicable to employers of 2 or more employees Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $13.73 The Michigan minimum wage is scheduled to increase on January 1, 2027 to $15.00 per hour and then will be adjusted annually based on a set formula. Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40 The State law excludes from coverage any employment that is subject to the federal Fair Labor Standards Act unless the State wage rate is higher than the federal rate.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.value: Within 20 calendar days after the date of hire or re-hire.

facts.summary: Michigan is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration

facts.summary: Michigan base new employer UI rate: 2.70%.

Rate basis: DOL base rate. It may exclude mandatory surcharges, fund-building rates and assessments; check the state agency or total_new_employer_rate where available.
